messages.content: Write the welcome page new engineers see on their first day at a software company. Around 250 words.

output:
249 words, and it passes the repo's own slopwatch gate clean.

---

# Welcome

Your laptop is on the desk. The password is on the card under the keyboard, and it expires in an hour, so start there.

Today has no deliverables. The one thing we ask you to finish by Friday is a change shipped to production. A typo fix, a log line, whatever you notice. It isn't a test of you. It's how we check that our onboarding docs still work, and new people find the broken steps faster than anyone.

A few things worth knowing early:

Ask questions in public channels, not DMs. A DM helps one person. The same question in #eng-help gets answered once and read for years. Nobody here keeps score of what you didn't know on day three.

Your manager is [name]. You'll meet for thirty minutes today and every week after. Bring what's blocking you; they'll bring the rest.

Code review here is slow on purpose. Expect comments. Most of them are questions rather than objections, and you can disagree with any of them in writing.

We deploy about forty times a day, so you will break something eventually. When it happens, say so in #incidents before you start fixing it. Our postmortems don't have names in them.

Lunch is whenever. Most of the team eats around 12:30 in the fourth-floor kitchen. Sit down with people you haven't met yet. The org chart makes more sense from a table than from a wiki page.

Read nothing else today. The rest keeps.

Welcome aboard.

---

The bracketed bits (manager name, channel names, floor, deploy count) are placeholders to swap for real values. Draft is at `/tmp/welcome.md` if you want it in the repo instead.
